newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end marginally up after profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end marginally up after profit-taking.

text.p: Thai stocks ended marginally up after losing most of the gains made on Wednesday amid profit-taking, brokers said.

The SET index, which moved in positive territory almost all day, slipped into negative zone less than 10 minutes before the market closed. It rebounded less than a minute before the session ended with the index up 0.32 point at 720.27 on active trade of 7.9 billion baht turnover.
"Investors earlier sold and took profit as they thought that prices of some bank and finance issues had risen reasonably in the past week," a broker said.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.03 point to 53.64.
Gainers slightly edged decliners 163 to 148 while 96 issues were unchanged.

"Despite a brief profit-taking towards the end of the session, the market sentiment in general was still good as there were buying orders from abroad," said Dusanee Klewpatinontha of Nithipat Capital.
Brokers said there were purchasing orders for some large capitalised banking and communication issues from Hong Kong and Singapore soon earlier in the day.
Brokers said investor confidence in the market was still good after a cabinet approval on Tuesday to float zero-coupon bonds to help the ailing property sector.
The banking sector gained most in terms of value, rising 1.05 percent, followed by the finance sector slipping 0.08 percent. The property sector dropped 2.74 percent.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, advancing 1.50 baht to 38.75. TelecomAsia retreated 0.75 to 42.
Support was seen by some brokers at the 700-point-level while resistance was viewed at 720 on Thursday.
